datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent in Juba Dhexe and Jhuba Hoose Regions, Somalia as of 07 November 2023
datasets.description: UNOSAT code FL20231105SOM This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters in Bu'aaler and Saakow District, Juba Dhexe Region and Afmadow District, Juba Hoose Region Somalia as observed from a Sentinel-1 image acquired on 07 November 2023 at 02:54 UTC. Within the analysed area of about 7,600 km², about 180 km² of land appear to be flooded. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT). Important note: Flood analysis from radar images may underestimate the presence of standing waters in built-up areas and densely vegetated areas due to backscattering properties of the radar signal.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extent-in-juba-dhexe-and-jhuba-hoose-regions-somalia-as-of-07-november-2023]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed Sentinel-1 radar imagery acquired on 7 November 2023 over Bu'aaler, Saakow, and Afmadow districts, comparing satellite images to detect notable changes in surface water extent. The analysis identified approximately 180 km² of flooded land within a 7,600 km² study area, with results delivered as vector geodatabase and shapefile formats for spatial analysis.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar imagery analyzed to detect surface water extent and map flooded areas through satellite image interpretation and change detection methodology
